findings: Observer failures can change application persistence and navigation. observe() synchronously calls a throwing native journal without isolation. In flush(), an exception from the settled observation enters the mutation-failure catch and removes the queue entry; enqueue() can skip flush(), and closeViewer() can skip closing the viewer. See vendor/helper/index.ts:9, vendor/helper/ios/CliqueNativeObserverModule.swift:36, vendor/helper/ios/ObservationJournal.swift:42, src/outbox.ts:13, src/outbox.ts:15 and src/Chat.tsx:27.

Search observations can report results that are not rendered. Offline cached matching accepts an empty query, the observation reports rows, but SearchBar receives an empty results array when text is empty. See src/cache.ts:7 and src/Search.tsx:6–9.

Conversation observations can retain removed rows: visible.map() falls back to the previous viewability item when its identity no longer exists in displayRows. A committed screen can therefore report an item absent from the committed list. See src/Chat.tsx:19 and src/Chat.tsx:37–39.

The oracle creates an ordinary fresh Bob session, performs only history queries afterward, exhausts the exclusive sequence cursor, preserves every returned occurrence and emits raw projected rows. Login's session creation is the required authentication write.

Under the supplied fixed environment, native/web clients resolve to the recorded origin, seed deployment targets the existing local backend, and backendArgv exactly matches the mandated operator-owned launcher.

Prepared iOS inputs reference this custody directory. The wrapper receives only $1 and explicitly builds Release for the generic iOS Simulator destination into the supplied DerivedData directory. Package and lockfile pins match Convex 1.45.0, Expo 57.0.22 and React Native 0.86.3.
Source qualification only: native accessibility exposure, runtime behavior and pixels are not established.
